newsitem.title: UK: IRA suspect loses German extradition battle.
newsitem.headline: IRA suspect loses German extradition battle.

text.p: Britain's High Court upheld an extradition request on Wednesday for pregnant IRA suspect Roisin McAliskey who is wanted in Germany for attempted murder in connection with a mortar attack on a British army base.

The two judges at the habeas corpus hearing ruled that Germany could seek her extradition. They rejected arguments that it was unlawful under the European Convention because Germany does not allow its own citizens to be extradited.
"It is our submission that it follows that Germany cannot require of the U.K. (United Kingdom) what the U.K. cannot require of Germany," her lawyer, Edward Fitzgerald, told the court.
McAliskey, who is six months pregnant, is the daughter of Bernadette McAliskey, nee Devlin, a former nationalist member of parliament and prominent republican in the 1960s.
McAliskey, 25, must appeal to the House of Lords, the country's highest court, if she wants to fight the decision.

Gareth Peirce, who is also representing her, criticised the decision. "Anyone's primary concern is that here is a young woman in poor health who is on a collision course between pregnancy and extradition," she said.
"Custody, extradition and successful delivery of the baby appear to be incompatible."

McAliskey was arrested in December along with James Curry, 28. Both are suspected of involvement in the attack on a British army base near the northwestern German town of Osnabrueck last June 26. No one was injured in the attack in which only one of three mortar bombs fired at the barracks exploded. The bomb which went off was short of its target.
It was the first IRA attack on continental Europe since the group broke a 17-month ceasefire last February.
McAliskey, who was refused bail, is being held in a high security prison. Her lawyer, who had requested bail, said there were complications with her pregnancy.
McAliskey's mother accused Britain of racism and inhumanity in its treatment of her daughter.
